title: lorastats v1
$comment: CANONICAL DIALECT: bare field names, integer values. Re-derived from the 29 Aug 2026 production sample, in which lorastats arrived in THREE mutually incompatible dialects in three consecutive records - bare/integer, bare/string ('176'), and lora_-prefixed/integer (lora_rx_nr_pkts) - all three carrying version:1, so nothing on the record discriminates them. Q15a was answered on 4 Sep 2026 (DL-105): ALL THREE known dialects are accepted and normalised to one typed row, which reverses ADR-007 §4 and supersedes DL-089. The enumeration is CLOSED AT THREE -- an unknown fourth still dead-letters. NOT YET BUILT: T-063 is what widens this schema and adds structural dialect detection, so today only the bare/integer dialect validates and the other two still dead-letter. That is a build state, not the decision. Bare/integer was chosen as the FIRST dialect encoded because it matches omsstats, which shares the same converter family; under DL-105 it stops being the only one. String counters are range-checked against the signed BIGINT maximum BEFORE conversion and dead-letter on overflow or a bad parse -- never zeroed, never truncated. rx_short_pkt, fsk_received and rx_type_arol are observed in production, are OPTIONAL because no record carries all three, and are typed so a dialect that sends them as strings still dead-letters. timespan is optional: the bare/string record omits it entirely.
